text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's president-elect Petar Stoyanov postponed a visit to Moscow scheduled to begin today because of Russia's President Boris Yeltsin's cold, Stoyanov's press office said.
-- The average monthly wage in Bulgaria this year was assumed at 34,783 levs in the 1997 draft budget approved by the outgoing government last week, government officials said.
-- An International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission is expected to arrive in Bulgaria immediately after a new cabinet is formed, IMF officials in Sofia said.

-- The ruling Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP) executive bureau said it would nominate outgoing Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev for a new prime minister following the resignation of Zhan Videnov in December.
-- Some 30,000 Bulgarians joined a protest rally in the second largest Bulgarian city of Plovdiv organised by the opposition with calls for early parliamentary elections.

-- Some $1 billion will be needed to complete construction of Bulgaria's second nuclear power plant at Belene on the Danube river according to an estimate made by Russian companies Atomenergoproject and Atomenergoexport and received at Bulgaria's National Electric Company.

-- The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said it had changed its method of daily calculation of the lev fixing against major currencies, effective from January 6, to achieve a more realistic reflection of the interbank foreign exchange market.

-- Bulgaria's biggest Confederation of Independent Trade Unions (CITU) is expected to support protest rallies acroos the country organised by the opposition with calls for early parliamentary elections, CITU leader Krastyo Petkov said.
-- The price of drinking water was raised by some 40 percent from January 1 due to a rise of electricity prices by 43 percent, Bulgaria's Construction ministry officials said.
